facts.ad: Andorra's coat of arms blends emblems of France and Spain—honoring its unique centuries-old rule by two co-princes.
facts.ae: The UAE's flag was designed in 1971 by a 19-year-old winner of a national contest using the four classic Pan-Arab colors.
facts.af: Afghanistan's traditional tricolor features a central emblem depicting a mosque pulpit, wheat sheaves, and rays of a rising sun.
facts.ag: Antigua and Barbuda's V-shape stands for victory, with a rising seven-point golden sun symbolizing the dawn of a new era.
facts.al: Albania's bold black double-headed eagle traces back to 15th-century national hero Skanderbeg—its native name means 'Land of the Eagles.'
facts.am: Armenia's bottom band isn't ordinary orange—its law officially names it 'tsiranaguyn' (apricot color), honoring Armenia's famous native fruit!
facts.ao: Angola's golden emblem pairs half a cogwheel with a machete and star to represent industrial workers and rural farmers.
facts.aq: Antarctica's blue-and-white map flag celebrates peaceful global scientific cooperation on Earth's only continent with no permanent residents.
facts.ar: Argentina's golden Sun of May has 32 alternating straight and wavy rays, inspired by the Incan sun god Inti.
facts.at: Austria's red-white-red triband is among Europe's oldest designs, linked to a 12th-century legend of Duke Leopold V's battle tunic.
facts.au: Australia's 7-pointed Commonwealth Star has one point for each of its six states plus a seventh for all its territories.
facts.aw: Aruba's sky-blue field and four-pointed red star celebrate the Caribbean Sea and the island's four main spoken languages.
facts.az: Azerbaijan's eight-pointed white star inside its turquoise-red-green stripes symbolizes the eight traditional branches of Turkic peoples.
facts.ba: Bosnia and Herzegovina's yellow triangle mirrors the rough shape of the country, framed by white stars inspired by Europe.
facts.bb: Barbados displays a broken black trident head—honoring Neptune's sea trident while symbolizing a clean break from colonial rule.
facts.bd: Bangladesh's red sun disc is intentionally shifted slightly toward the flagpole so it looks dead-center when rippling in the wind.
facts.be: Belgium uses an unusually square 13:15 official ratio—narrower than almost every other tricolor flag on Earth.
facts.bf: Burkina Faso's single golden star sits between red and green bands, honoring the nation's 1984 renaming to 'Land of Upright People.'
facts.bg: Bulgaria adapted the Pan-Slavic tricolor in 1879 by swapping blue for emerald green—marking a fresh start after regaining independence.
facts.bh: Bahrain reduced its jagged hoist border to exactly five white triangles in 2002 to represent the Five Pillars of Islam.
facts.bi: Burundi's three red stars inside a white circle stand for its national motto: Unity, Work, and Progress.
facts.bj: Benin first hoisted this Pan-African layout in 1959, swapped to a solid green flag with a red star in 1975, and joyfully restored the original in 1990!
facts.bm: Bermuda's red ensign displays a white lion holding a shield showing the 1609 shipwreck of the Sea Venture that settled the islands.
facts.bn: Brunei's crest features a royal umbrella, upturned wings, and guiding hands over a crescent inscribed with a motto of peace.
facts.bo: Bolivia officially flies TWO national flags side by side: this 1851 red-yellow-green tricolor and the vibrant 49-square indigenous Wiphala!
facts.br: Brazil's 27 stars map the exact sky over Rio de Janeiro at 8:30 AM on November 15, 1889, the morning it became a republic.
facts.bs: The Bahamas' aquamarine stripes represent sparkling island waters framing a golden sand bar and a black triangle of unity.
facts.bt: Bhutan's flag features Druk, the white Thunder Dragon, clutching four jewels in its claws to symbolize the kingdom's wealth.
facts.bw: Botswana's sky blue honors precious rain ('Pula'—also its motto and currency!), while the black-and-white stripe symbolizes racial harmony and echoes its national animal, the zebra.
facts.by: Belarus's vertical hoist band showcases a traditional red-and-white woven 'rushnyk' folk textile pattern dating back centuries.
facts.bz: Belize has the only national flag featuring human beings as a major design element—two woodcutters beside a mahogany tree.
facts.ca: Canada's 1965 flag beat thousands of public designs—its 11-pointed maple leaf was wind-tunnel tested to stay legible from afar.
facts.cd: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's red diagonal stripe edged in yellow cuts across sky blue to symbolize peace and vast natural wealth.
facts.cf: The Central African Republic combined French tricolor hues with Pan-African colors, bridged vertically by a bold red center stripe.
facts.cg: The Republic of the Congo uses a diagonal layout of green, yellow, and red—unique among Pan-African tricolors for its slanted bands.
facts.ch: Switzerland flies one of only two square sovereign flags—and inspired the Red Cross emblem simply by inverting Switzerland's red-and-white colors!
facts.ci: Côte d'Ivoire flips Ireland's tricolor order—putting orange on the flagpole side for the northern savanna and green on the fly for coastal forests.
facts.cl: Chile's 'La Estrella Solitaria' (The Lone Star) predates the Texas flag by over 20 years—adopted in 1817!
facts.cm: Cameroon replaced its two stars with a single centered gold star in 1975 to symbolize the unity of its regions.
facts.cn: China's large golden star is flanked by four smaller stars whose points each tilt gently toward the center of the main star.
facts.co: Colombia's top yellow stripe is double-wide—representing abundant gold and sunshine above blue oceans and crimson courage.
facts.cr: Costa Rica added a double-wide red stripe to the Central American blue-and-white banner in 1848, inspired by the French tricolor.
facts.cu: Cuba's 'La Estrella Solitaria' has five stripes for its historic provinces and inspired the inverse-colored flag of Puerto Rico.
facts.cv: Cabo Verde's ring of ten golden stars represents its ten main Atlantic volcanic islands floating over deep blue ocean.
facts.cw: Curaçao's two white stars represent the main island and uninhabited Little Curaçao, separated from the sea by a golden bar of sunshine.
facts.cy: Cyprus is one of only two nations to put its own geographic map on its flag—colored copper because the island's name comes from copper!
facts.cz: Czechia kept the blue triangle of the former Czechoslovakia—making it one of Europe's most recognizable geometric designs.
facts.de: Germany's black-red-gold tricolor traces back to 19th-century student unity movements advocating for a free, unified republic.
facts.dj: Djibouti's sky-blue-over-green banner was first hoisted at midnight on June 27, 1977—adapted straight from its independence movement's emblem.
facts.dk: Denmark's Dannebrog is the oldest continuously used state flag in the world—legend says it fell from the sky in 1219!
facts.dm: Dominica is one of the very few national flags containing purple—found on the chest of its native Sisserou parrot—once rarer than gold!
facts.do: The Dominican Republic is the only national flag in the world that features an open Bible inside its center coat of arms.
facts.dz: Algeria's red star and crescent sit squarely across the border of green and white halves, representing peace and heritage.
facts.ec: Ecuador shares Colombia's double-wide yellow tricolor but adds a soaring Andean condor perched atop its detailed national shield.
facts.ee: Estonia's blue, black, and white stripes famously evoke its winter landscape: crisp blue sky, dark pine forests, and white snow.
facts.eg: Egypt's golden Eagle of Saladin stands centered on a white band, gazing left as an ancient emblem of strength and sovereignty.
facts.er: Eritrea's golden olive wreath encircles an upright branch with exactly 30 leaves—marking the thirty years of its independence struggle.
facts.es: Spain's bright red-yellow-red 'Rojigualda' was chosen in 1785 by King Charles III so Spanish ships could be spotted easily at sea!
facts.et: Ethiopia's green-yellow-red banner is the historic inspiration for the Pan-African colors adopted by dozens of nations across Africa.
facts.eu: The European Union's circle of 12 gold stars never changes when members join—12 was chosen as a timeless symbol of harmony and perfection.
facts.fi: Finland's crisp blue Nordic cross on pure white symbolizes the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' blanketed in bright winter snow.
facts.fj: Fiji's sky-blue shield carries sugarcane, a coconut palm, bananas, and a white dove holding an olive branch.
facts.fm: Micronesia's four white stars arranged in a diamond represent its four constituent Pacific island states: Chuuk, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and Yap.
facts.fo: The Faroe Islands' 'Merkið' was first designed by Faroese students in Copenhagen in 1919 and features a red-on-blue Nordic cross.
facts.fr: France's blue-white-red Tricolore became the blueprint for dozens of modern vertical-striped national flags worldwide.
facts.ga: Gabon's golden middle stripe represents the Equator cutting right across the country between lush green rainforests and the Atlantic Ocean.
facts.gb: The Union Jack layers St. George's, St. Andrew's, and St. Patrick's crosses—pinwheeling the red saltire so Scotland and Ireland share equal rank (giving it a right side up!).
facts.gd: Grenada features a golden nutmeg pod on its left triangle, celebrating its nickname as the Caribbean's 'Island of Spice.'
facts.ge: Georgia's 'Five Cross Flag' revives a medieval 14th-century banner with one large St. George cross flanked by four Bolnisi crosses.
facts.gh: Ghana was the first independent sub-Saharan nation to adopt the Pan-African colors, adding its iconic centered Black Star of Freedom.
facts.gi: Gibraltar's red castle with three towers and a hanging golden key symbolizes its historic role as the strategic 'Key to the Mediterranean.'
facts.gl: Greenland is the only Nordic flag without a cross—its inverted red-and-white circle depicts the midnight sun setting over Arctic ice.
facts.gm: The Gambia's white-bordered blue center stripe literally represents the Gambia River winding between sun-drenched savanna and fertile forests.
facts.gn: Guinea reverses Mali's stripe order—placing red on the flagpole side, yellow in the center, and green on the outer fly.
facts.gq: Equatorial Guinea's center shield features a giant silk-cotton tree beneath six gold stars representing its mainland and five islands.
facts.gr: Greece's nine blue-and-white stripes match the nine syllables of its classic freedom motto: 'Eleftheria i Thanatos' (Freedom or Death).
facts.gt: Guatemala's sky-blue stripes frame its national bird, the resplendent quetzal, perched on a scroll marking its 1821 independence.
facts.gu: Guam's almond-shaped center seal echoes the shape of ancient Chamorro slingstones, framing a palm tree and sailing canoe.
facts.gw: Guinea-Bissau's layout pairs a vertical red hoist band with yellow-over-green horizontal bars and a centered Black Star of Africa.
facts.gy: Nicknamed 'The Golden Arrowhead,' Guyana's flag was designed by Whitney Smith—the scholar who literally coined the word 'vexillology'!
facts.hk: Hong Kong's white five-petal bauhinia flower blooms on crimson, with a tiny red star tucked neatly inside each petal.
facts.hn: Honduras's five turquoise stars form an X representing the five historic nations of the Federal Republic of Central America.
facts.hr: Croatia's iconic red-and-white checkered shield ('šahovnica') is crowned by five smaller shields representing its historic regions.
facts.ht: Haiti's 1803 blue-and-red banner was famously born during its independence revolution by ripping the white stripe right out of the French tricolor!
facts.hu: During Hungary's 1956 uprising, protesters famously cut the Soviet-era crest out of this tricolor—making the 'flag with a hole' a lasting icon of freedom.
facts.id: Indonesia's 'Sang Saka Merah-Putih' traces its iconic red-and-white horizontal bands back over 700 years to the maritime Majapahit Empire of Java!
facts.ie: Ireland's green and orange represent its Catholic and Protestant traditions, joined by white in the center standing for lasting peace.
facts.il: Israel's blue stripes and centered Star of David draw directly from the design of the traditional woven tallit prayer shawl.
facts.im: The Isle of Man's three spinning armored legs (triskelion) pair with the motto: 'Whichever way you throw it, it will stand!'
facts.in: India's center navy-blue Ashoka Chakra has exactly 24 spokes—symbolizing the continuous forward motion of righteous law.
facts.iq: Iraq's tricolor carries the green Arabic inscription 'Allahu Akbar' written in bold traditional Kufic script across the white center.
facts.ir: Iran's center tulip-shaped emblem is flanked by 22 tiny geometric repetitions of 'Allahu Akbar' tucked along the edges of the green and red bands.
facts.is: Iceland's red-on-white Nordic cross over deep blue symbolizes volcanic fire, glacial ice, and the surrounding North Atlantic Ocean.
facts.it: Italy's green-white-red 'Il Tricolore' debuted in 1797 and inspired legends of green hills, snowy Alps, and heartfelt devotion.
facts.jm: Jamaica has the only national flag on Earth containing zero red, white, or blue—honoring its sun, green land, and resilience.
facts.jo: Jordan's seven-pointed white star stands for the seven opening verses of the Quran and the unity of the Arab people.
facts.jp: Japan's 'Nisshōki' (sun-mark flag) flew for centuries, yet its exact 2:3 geometry and crimson shade weren't standardized by law until 1999.
facts.ke: Kenya's centered traditional Maasai shield and crossed spears symbolize the defense of freedom across its black, red, and green bands.
facts.kg: Kyrgyzstan's 40-ray golden sun represents 40 ancient united tribes, framing the lattice roof crown ('tunduk') of a traditional yurt.
facts.kh: Cambodia is one of the very few nations to feature a real landmark on its flag—the towering stone silhouette of Angkor Wat.
facts.ki: Kiribati shows a golden frigatebird soaring above a 17-ray rising sun and Pacific waves right near the International Date Line.
facts.km: Comoros's four horizontal stripes and four white stars each represent one of the archipelago's four main Indian Ocean islands.
facts.kn: Saint Kitts and Nevis's two white stars stand for hope and liberty as well as the twin Caribbean islands themselves.
facts.kp: North Korea's red star in a white disc sits slightly left of center between wide red, thin white, and deep blue horizontal stripes.
facts.kr: South Korea's four corner trigrams symbolize heaven, earth, water, and fire balancing the red-and-blue Taegeuk of cosmic harmony.
facts.kw: Kuwait's black trapezoid on the left distinguishes its Pan-Arab tricolor—its colors were inspired by a famous 14th-century Arabic poem.
facts.kz: Kazakhstan's soaring steppe eagle flies beneath a 32-ray golden sun, bordered on the hoist by a traditional Kazakh ornamental motif.
facts.la: Laos's large white circle represents a bright full moon glowing over the Mekong River and the unity of its people.
facts.lb: Lebanon's central green cedar honors the ancient biblical cedars of Mount Lebanon, symbols of endurance and immortality.
facts.lc: Saint Lucia's sleek geometric black-and-gold triangles represent the Pitons—twin volcanic peaks rising dramatically from the cerulean sea.
facts.li: Liechtenstein added its golden prince's crown in 1937 right after realizing at the 1936 Olympics that its flag matched Haiti's!
facts.lk: Sri Lanka's golden sword-bearing lion is framed by four Bo leaves representing Buddhist kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity.
facts.lr: Liberia's eleven red-and-white stripes honor the eleven signers of its 1847 Declaration of Independence, with a single star for Africa's first republic.
facts.ls: Lesotho's centered black emblem is a 'mokorotlo'—the iconic woven conical straw hat worn by the Basotho people.
facts.lt: Lithuania chose its warm yellow, green, and red palette in 1918 to echo traditional woven folk textiles—standing out distinctly from Europe's usual tricolors.
facts.lu: Luxembourg uses a bright sky-blue lower band and wider 3:5 ratio to stand apart from the deeper cobalt blue of the Netherlands.
facts.lv: Latvia's unique deep carmine 'Latvian red' in a 2:1:2 band ratio comes from a 13th-century banner recorded in medieval chronicles.
facts.ly: Libya's 1951 black-red-green design with a white star and crescent honors its three historic regions: Cyrenaica, Fezzan, and Tripolitania.
facts.ma: Morocco's dark green five-pointed star—known as the Seal of Solomon—has appeared on its bold crimson banner since 1915.
facts.mc: Monaco's red-and-white colors come from the ruling House of Grimaldi (1339)—and its squarer 4:5 proportions set it apart from Indonesia's 2:3 flag.
facts.md: Moldova's coat of arms features a golden eagle holding an olive branch and scepter over a shield bearing an ancient aurochs head.
facts.me: Montenegro's gold-bordered crimson flag displays a crowned double-headed eagle shielding a golden lion on a green-and-blue crest.
facts.mg: Madagascar's white vertical bar paired with red and green bands echoes the classic red-and-white royal colors of the Merina Kingdom.
facts.mh: The Marshall Islands' 24-pointed white star has four extra-long rays marking both the compass directions and the islands' equatorial home.
facts.mk: North Macedonia's bold eight-rayed golden sun on red is inspired by the line 'new sun of liberty' in its national anthem.
facts.ml: Mali's original 1959 flag featured a black stick-figure dancer ('Kanaga') in the yellow center before switching to this clean vertical tricolor in 1961!
facts.mm: Myanmar replaced its 1974 blue-canton flag in 2010 with this bold yellow-green-red tricolor crowned by a single giant white star.
facts.mn: Mongolia's golden 'Soyombo' column on the hoist packs ancient symbols for fire, sun, moon, earth, water, and yin-yang balance!
facts.mo: Macau's stylized white lotus blossom blooms over a silhouette of the Governor Nobre de Carvalho Bridge and ocean waves.
facts.mr: Mauritania added top and bottom red stripes in 2017—leaving Jamaica as the sole national flag on Earth with no red, white, or blue!
facts.mt: Malta displays the silver George Cross awarded to the entire island in 1942 for collective bravery during World War II.
facts.mu: Mauritius is one of the very few nations with four equal horizontal stripes—red, blue, yellow, and green—representing its island life.
facts.mv: The Maldives' green rectangle framed in bold crimson represents lush palm islands and heritage, centered with a white crescent.
facts.mw: Malawi's rising red sun with 31 rays atop a black band symbolizes the dawn of hope and freedom across the African continent.
facts.mx: Mexico's emblem shows the Aztec founding prophecy: an eagle perched on a cactus devouring a serpent, marking where to build their capital.
facts.my: Malaysia's 'Jalur Gemilang' (Stripes of Glory) has 14 stripes and a 14-point star honoring its 13 states plus federal territories.
facts.mz: Mozambique's unique emblem layers an open book, a hoe, and an AK-47 over a yellow star—symbolizing education, agriculture, and defense.
facts.na: Namibia's 12-rayed golden sun shines over the arid Namib Desert, cut diagonally by a red stripe symbolizing the nation's people.
facts.ne: Niger's centered orange sun disc sits between bright orange savanna sands above and fertile green Niger River valleys below.
facts.ng: Nigeria's symmetrical green-white-green flag was designed in 1959 by 23-year-old engineering student Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi.
facts.ni: Nicaragua is one of the very few national flags to contain purple—tucked inside a tiny rainbow arching over five volcanoes in its seal.
facts.nl: The Netherlands flies the world's oldest tricolor still in use—originally orange-white-blue before sailors switched to fade-resistant red dye!
facts.no: Vexillology fans call Norway the 'Mother of Flags'—you can crop Indonesia, Poland, Finland, France, Netherlands, and Thailand right out of it!
facts.np: Nepal's is the world's only non-rectangular national flag—its twin triangles represent the Himalayas, with sun and moon for eternal endurance.
facts.nr: Nauru's 12-pointed white star sits just below a golden equator line—literally mapping the tiny Pacific island's exact spot 1° south of the Equator!
facts.nz: New Zealand's Southern Cross features four red stars with white borders—the fastest way to distinguish it from Australia's white stars.
facts.om: Oman's white emblem in the top-left canton combines two crossed traditional swords behind a curved 'khanjar' ceremonial dagger.
facts.pa: Panama's clean four-quarter design balances a blue star for honesty and a red star for law across opposing fields of peace.
facts.pe: A beloved Peruvian legend popularized by a 1917 short story says General San Martín picked red and white after dreaming of flamingos taking flight!
facts.pg: Papua New Guinea's flag was designed in 1971 by 15-year-old student Susan Karike—featuring the Southern Cross and a golden bird-of-paradise!
facts.ph: If the Philippines flips its flag upside-down with the red stripe on top, it officially signals a state of war!
facts.pk: Pakistan's white vertical bar honors religious minorities alongside the green majority, crowned by a crescent of progress and star of light.
facts.pl: Poland's crisp white-over-red banner reverses Indonesia and Monaco—its heraldic colors trace back to a medieval white eagle on crimson.
facts.pr: Puerto Rico's 1895 banner intentionally inverted Cuba's red-and-blue colors to express historic sisterhood between the two Caribbean islands.
facts.ps: Palestine's Pan-Arab tricolor of black, white, and green with a red hoist triangle traces directly to the historic 1916 Arab Revolt banner.
facts.pt: Portugal's coat of arms rests on a golden armillary sphere—an Age-of-Discovery nautical astrolabe celebrating its maritime navigators!
facts.pw: Palau's off-center golden disc isn't the sun—it's the full moon, a treasured symbol of peace, good harvests, and coastal tides.
facts.py: Paraguay has one of the only national flags on Earth with different emblems on each side—its national crest on the front and a lion seal on the back!
facts.qa: Qatar flies the world's longest national flag ratio (11:28)—more than twice as wide as tall—with nine white teeth marking its 1916 treaty.
facts.ro: Romania's tricolor debuted in 1848—and during its 1989 revolution, protesters famously cut the old coat of arms right out of the center, waving flags with a hole!
facts.rs: Serbia's Pan-Slavic tricolor bears a crowned white double-headed eagle with four fire-steels surrounding a cross on its crimson shield.
facts.ru: Russia's white-blue-red maritime banner was championed by Tsar Peter the Great in the late 1600s and inspired the Pan-Slavic flag palette.
facts.rw: Rwanda's 24-ray golden sun tucked in the upper-right sky-blue band was introduced in 2001 to symbolize enlightenment and national unity.
facts.sa: Saudi Arabia's flag is sewn from two identical pieces back-to-back so its calligraphy reads right-to-left on both sides—and it never flies at half-mast.
facts.sb: The Solomon Islands' five white stars represent its five original island provinces, divided by a golden diagonal sunbeam.
facts.sc: Seychelles' five bold diagonal rays sweep upward from the bottom-left corner to evoke a young island nation striding into the future.
facts.sd: Sudan's green hoist triangle paired with red, white, and black stripes honors agriculture, progress, peace, and the nation's historic name.
facts.se: Sweden's golden Nordic cross on blue dates to the 16th century and helped inspire the beloved cross template shared across Northern Europe.
facts.sg: Singapore's crescent represents a young rising nation, while its five stars stand for democracy, peace, progress, justice, and equality.
facts.si: Slovenia's shield depicts Mount Triglav—its iconic three-peaked Alpine summit—beneath three golden six-pointed stars of the Counts of Celje.
facts.sk: Slovakia's white double cross stands atop three blue mountain peaks representing the Tatra, Fatra, and Mátra ranges.
facts.sl: Sierra Leone's green, white, and blue banner was first raised at midnight in April 1961—its three colors echo the shield of its official coat of arms.
facts.sm: San Marino's shield displays three plumed stone towers representing the three medieval mountaintop fortresses guarding Mount Titano.
facts.sn: Senegal's green center star distinguishes its green-yellow-red tricolor from neighboring Mali—symbolizing unity and open hope.
facts.so: Somalia's sky-blue field honors the United Nations' role in its 1960 independence, centered with a five-pointed Star of Unity.
facts.sr: Suriname chose its five-stripe design via a 1975 national competition, uniting its major political movements beneath one centered golden star.
facts.ss: South Sudan—the world's newest UN member state (2011)—features six colors, including a gold Star of Bethlehem inside a blue triangle.
facts.st: São Tomé and Príncipe's two black stars represent its two main volcanic islands nestled along the Equator in the Gulf of Guinea.
facts.sv: El Salvador's center seal displays five green volcanoes rising from the sea beneath a Phrygian liberty cap and tiny rainbow.
facts.sy: Syria's green-white-black flag with three red stars—originally designed in 1932 for independence—was officially readopted in late 2024.
facts.sz: Eswatini displays a traditional Nguni oxhide war shield crossed by two spears and a staff adorned with royal blue feather tassels.
facts.td: Chad blended France's blue with Pan-African gold and red in 1959—accidentally creating a near-identical twin to Romania's flag on another continent!
facts.tg: Togo's official flag proportions follow the mathematical Golden Ratio (~1:1.618)—making it one of the most precisely proportioned flags on Earth!
facts.th: Thailand's symmetrical red-white-blue-white-red 'Thong Trairong' was introduced in 1917—with blue symbolizing the monarchy at the center.
facts.tj: Tajikistan's golden crown topped by an arc of seven stars honors the country's name (linked to 'crown') and the lucky number seven.
facts.tl: Timor-Leste's overlapping black and yellow triangles lead into bright red, guided by a tilted white star representing light and peace.
facts.tm: Turkmenistan boasts one of the world's most intricate flags—displaying five traditional woven carpet 'guls' (tribal medallions) down the hoist!
facts.tn: Tunisia's red crescent and star inside a white disc dates back to 1827, making it one of the oldest continuously used designs in North Africa.
facts.to: Tonga moved its red cross into the top-left canton in 1875 specifically so its national flag wouldn't be mistaken for the Red Cross emblem!
facts.tr: Turkey's iconic white crescent and star evolved from historic Ottoman naval banners and inspired similar celestial emblems worldwide.
facts.tt: Trinidad and Tobago's bold white-edged black diagonal slash cuts across crimson to symbolize earth, water, and fire.
facts.tv: Tuvalu's nine golden stars are mapped in the exact real-world geographic layout of the nation's nine Pacific islands!
facts.tw: Taiwan's flag features a 12-ray white sun in a blue canton, representing the twelve traditional hours of the day and twelve months of the year.
facts.tz: Tanzania's diagonal black band edged in gold merges the green-and-blue flag colors of Tanganyika and Zanzibar after their 1964 union.
facts.ua: Ukraine's poetic blue-over-gold design represents vast open skies stretching over endless golden wheat fields.
facts.ug: Uganda's centerpiece is a grey crowned crane—its national bird—shown raising one leg forward to symbolize a nation marching ahead.
facts.un: The United Nations flag maps all inhabited continents centered on the North Pole—so no single nation sits 'on top'—cradled by olive branches.
facts.us: The U.S. flag has been officially redesigned 27 times—one of the highest counts in history—growing from 13 stars in 1777 to 50 stars in 1960!
facts.uy: Uruguay's 16-ray golden Sun of May sits beside nine blue-and-white stripes representing its nine original historic departments.
facts.uz: Uzbekistan's 12 white stars represent the 12 months and zodiac signs, arranged above blue sky, white peace, and green nature bands.
facts.va: Vatican City's crossed gold and silver keys represent the Keys of Heaven beneath the papal tiara—flying on a rare 1:1 square banner.
facts.vc: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines arranges three emerald diamonds in a 'V'—celebrating its nickname as the 'Gems of the Antilles.'
facts.ve: Venezuela's arc of eight white stars honors its seven original independence provinces plus Guayana, curving across a deep blue stripe.
facts.vn: Vietnam's bold five-pointed gold star on crimson represents the unity of farmers, workers, intellectuals, youth, and soldiers.
facts.vu: Vanuatu's black triangle holds a coiled wild boar's tusk (a traditional symbol of prosperity) encircling two crossed namele fern fronds of peace.
facts.ws: Samoa's five white Southern Cross stars include four big stars and one smaller star tucked inside a navy canton over red.
facts.xk: Kosovo's flag displays a golden silhouette map of its territory beneath an arc of six white stars representing its six major ethnic groups.
facts.ye: Yemen's clean red, white, and black horizontal bands unified North and South Yemen in 1990 using classic Pan-Arab colors.
facts.za: South Africa's 1994 'temporary' flag became permanent by popular demand—its sweeping Y-shape symbolizes diverse peoples walking one road ahead.
facts.zm: Zambia puts all its stripes and a soaring golden African fish eagle on the outer fly side—an unusual reverse-weighted layout in vexillology!
facts.zw: Zimbabwe's red star frames the carved soapstone 'Zimbabwe Bird'—a national treasure discovered among the medieval ruins of Great Zimbabwe.
